references.text: The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and his sons from the people of Israel, confirming their service role.
The dedication of the Levites to Aaron to serve in the tabernacle and assist the priests in their work.
The Levites were to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony to prevent wrath from falling upon the congregation of Israel.
The atonement made by the priests for the people to stop the plague that struck the people of Israel.
The service of the Levites as helpers to Aaron and his sons at the tent of meeting.
The people of Israel must not approach the tent of meeting, lest they incur sin and die; the Levites are to carry out the service.
A warning that the priests must bear holy guilt when approaching the altar, so that they do not die.
Ransom money for atonement over the people of Israel to prevent plague.
Nadab and Abihu died when they approached the Lord in an unauthorized manner, a warning about the consequences of approaching the sanctuary improperly.
The men of Beth-Shemesh were struck down because they looked into the ark of the Lord, an example of plague when approaching holy things.
Uzzah died when he touched the ark of God, a warning against approaching the sanctuary in the wrong way.
